title: arXiv Biology & Biomedicine — Daily, 2026-11-04
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this relevance-ranked snapshot is not a popularity ranking. arXiv is incomplete biomedical coverage, and computational, simulated, retrospective, and experimental evidence are distinguished rather than treated as interchangeable.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Latest announcement batch: Wednesday, 4 November 2026. Six notable papers, led by prospective protein-binder design, DNA-design benchmarking, and protein conformational modeling. Spoken agenda: what biological sequence and structure models can do, what has been tested experimentally, and where the evidence remains bounded. arXiv has no official trending chart; this is a relevance-ranked snapshot, not a popularity ranking, and arXiv omits much of the biomedical preprint literature.

sections.title: ProteoCraft: Protein Design as Proposal-Verification Search
sections.abstract: Introduces a tree-search framework for de novo binder design and reports computational comparisons across 14 design settings plus prospective binding assays for PD-L1 miniproteins and IFNAR2 VHHs.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose using diffusion-model structural gradients to guide search while independent structure-model inference verifies candidates; they report an 82.9% PD-L1 miniprotein binding hit rate, a best measured KD of 0.879 nM, and binding for designed IFNAR2 VHH.
sections.unique_caveat: The experimental validation is limited to the tested targets and designs; the authors say specificity, biological activity, and generalization to additional targets require further characterization. Binding alone does not establish therapeutic efficacy.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Three-category cross-listing; 14 design settings; prospective synthesis and binding measurements, including 29 binding hits among 35 PD-L1 miniprotein candidates.

sections.title: BEND 2.0: Benchmarking the Capabilities Needed to Design DNA
sections.abstract: Introduces an eight-task benchmark across five experimental datasets to test genomic models' DNA mutation-effect prediction and sequence-design capabilities.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that fitted linear readouts can match or exceed native model outputs and transfer across some genes and assays, while context-specific effects and mutation interactions remain difficult.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a retrospective benchmark on existing experimental datasets, not prospective validation of newly designed DNA; the authors caution that results may not generalize uniformly across populations or biological settings.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Three-category breadth including genomics and quantitative biology; eight tasks/five experimental datasets; public code and leaderboard.

sections.title: Ablating Design Choices for Protein Ensemble Generators Across Structural Regimes
sections.abstract: Ablates design choices in a protein conformational-ensemble generator and compares generated ensembles with experimental SAXS and NMR chemical-shift data across ordered, disordered, multi-domain, and transitional proteins.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors find training-source choices matter more than several tested architectural choices; fragment-assembled disorder ensembles improve chemical-shift agreement, while mixing sources moderates the SAXS trade-off.
sections.unique_caveat: Authors note approximate training sources, unquantified back-mapping error, limited observables, and small non-ordered SAXS groups (34–42 proteins per cell, three seeds per variant); compactness agreement is not proof of fold correctness.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Biomolecular and machine-learning categories; experimental SAXS and NMR observables; paper states small non-ordered SAXS subgroups and three seeds per variant.

sections.title: Predicting protein structures at any folding stage from sequence
sections.abstract: Presents FoldScape, a sequence-conditioned model that generates coarse-grained protein conformational ensembles at a specified folding fraction, covering stages from collapsed coil toward near-native globules.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report about an order-of-magnitude greater folding-coordinate coverage than the tested AlphaFold 3 ensembles at matched sample size, while AlphaFold 3 better anchors the immediate native vicinity.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported ensembles are coarse-grained Cα models trained on simulated folding/unfolding trajectories; the abstract does not establish experimental accuracy for intermediate conformations, and the authors describe the methods as complementary.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in biomolecules and AI; evaluated 20 human proteins of 36–857 residues against seed-varied AlphaFold 3 ensembles.

sections.title: iGC: Antibody Optimization via Reinforcement Learning over a Learned Somatic Hypermutation Prior
sections.abstract: Presents a two-stage reinforcement-learning framework that learns a somatic-hypermutation prior from B-cell lineage data and uses it to guide antigen-specific antibody sequence optimization.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that their learned prior more than doubles the strongest baseline on mutation-site prediction and that RL optimization retains sequence-structure signals while balancing predicted reward and diversity.
sections.unique_caveat: The evaluation relies on deep-mutational-scanning-derived rewards rather than direct binding measurements of newly generated candidates, so experimental affinity improvement is not established.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Biomolecular relevance and machine-learning cross-listing; reports tests of mutation prediction, SHM consistency, reward optimization, and diversity.

sections.title: Empirical Bayes Flow Matching for Continuous Cryo-EM Heterogeneity
sections.abstract: Proposes an empirical-Bayes flow-matching method to infer continuous distributions of protein conformations from indirect observations, including simulated cryo-EM projections.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report recovering continuous protein-conformation distributions directly in atomic-coordinate space without pretraining on clean structures.
sections.unique_caveat: The cryo-EM demonstration uses simulated data and known poses; performance on real particle stacks, where poses and experimental effects are uncertain, remains to be established.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in biomolecules and machine learning; arXiv comment reports NeurIPS 2026 acceptance; cryo-EM test uses simulated data with known poses.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.content: Protein design pipelines combine broad computational search with targeted experimental checks, as in ProteoCraft; iGC shares the antibody-optimization goal but reports computational rewards rather than binding assays. Protein modeling moves toward ensembles: the protein-ensemble ablation study compares with SAXS/NMR, FoldScape generates coarse-grained folding-stage ensembles, and EB-FM's cryo-EM demonstration is simulated. Genomic foundation models are evaluated for intervention selection in BEND 2.0, whose retrospective benchmark reports both useful signals and gaps in context-specific and interaction prediction.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.content: Follow-up directions suggested by the papers: test ProteoCraft binders for off-target binding, functional activity, and generalization across independent targets; synthesize blinded iGC candidates and compare measured binding with DMS-derived reward. Prospectively test BEND 2.0 model-selected DNA edits in held-out genes and cell contexts, including combined mutations. For protein ensembles, add orthogonal observables, partially ordered proteins, back-mapping uncertainty estimates, and more replicates; compare FoldScape's intermediate-state predictions with independent experimental measurements. Evaluate EB-FM on real cryo-EM particle stacks with unknown poses and compare recovered heterogeneity against established workflows.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: This batch combines computational protein and DNA design with increasingly explicit modeling of conformational ensembles. ProteoCraft stands out for prospective binder assays, while several other contributions remain supported mainly by retrospective benchmarks or simulations. Read the performance claims within those evidence boundaries; none alone establishes clinical benefit.
